title: 1.b4???
transcript: The opponent decides to play a very weird first move, the Polish opening, which technically already gives me an advantage. But I know that this is a strong opponent [music] and that he knows what he's doing. And in fact, later in the game, I actually find myself having to defend against a checkmating attack. But thankfully, I just have enough space to shuffle my king back and forth and not get checkmated. And once I [music] manage to get the queens off the board, there is going to be no attack left for him. And actually the tables are turned after this move, allowing me to trade on my terms and play this fork, winning an exchange. So now I have a rook for a bishop, but I only have a couple of seconds left on the clock. So I really need to speed up and I start blitzing out moves just to farm some time. But playing this quickly inevitably leads to more mistakes and eventually we land in a position where I cannot prevent him from winning my black pawn on the edge of the board. His king is coming in and my rook cannot defend the pawn in any way. I realize I messed up. So, I have to give up my dreams of winning the game and I have to retreat trying to desperately stop the pawns. Luckily, I managed to run all the way back with my king just in time. [music] And now, after he goes up with the king, I'm going to be able to infiltrate. And no matter what he does on the next move, I'm going to sacrifice the rook for a drawn endame. There is an outside pawn and my king can run to the corner. So, this is a draw.
